criteria.criterion: `transition` lib param is `force: str | None` (reason-carrying), matching `claim`; `force: bool` and `force_close` are removed (grep shows no live `force_close` / `force: bool` param on `transition`).
Bare `--force` -> "(no reason given)" and `--force=<reason>` -> that reason, IDENTICALLY for `claim` and `transition` (interface tests).
The transition CLI no longer uses `--reason` as the force-bypass note; `--reason` feeds only close_reason (behavior-change test).
`force is not None` drives the bypass of BOTH the start-work and completion-verify close gates for `transition` (tests).
Legacy `force_close=` / `force=True` calls WARN via rebar._deprecations and map to the new `force` string (unit tests).
The in-memory force-reason concept is spelled `force_reason` across transition + claim internals; the persisted `force_close_reason` status key is retained (grep + a reducer back-compat test pass).

Every transition/claim guidance string (gates.py override hint, txn.py override hints, transition.py usage/help) shows only the `--force[=<reason>]` pattern; no `transition --force --reason=` or `--reason`-as-force-note wording remains (grep).
